title: A new high breakout rule on gold made 34% while just holding the same fund made 551%
author: person-person12
selftext:
Gold is at records and most of the charts on my feed right now are somebody buying the breakout, so i ran the rule people actually describe and then put the boring version next to it.

**The rule:** GLD daily candles, buy the close when it prints a new 250 day high while price is above its 50 day average, sell on the first close back below that average. No target, one position at a time, no borrowing. Late November 2005 to the end of March 2026, $10,000 to start, commission and slippage charged on both sides of every trade. The gold history i test on in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) starts at the fund's first day in 2004, so the window is basically its whole life.

**44 trades, 45.5% wins, profit factor 1.41, finished at $13,442.** Up 34.4% net, 33% max drawdown, with $515 of it paid out in costs.

Then the same window, buy once on the first day and hold until the end: **$65,175, up 551.8%,** 42% max drawdown. Entry 49.50, exit 408.22, one trade.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

So the rule works in the sense people mean when they say a rule works. Positive profit factor over twenty years, a shallower drawdown than holding, and it **took zero trades in 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015,** which is the stretch gold spent going down and the entire reason anybody bolts a moving average onto anything. Worst year 2009 at -$2,025, best year 2025 at +$1,713. One trade out of 44 ever hit its stop, the other 43 exited on the average and ran at a 1.99 profit factor between them.

It still finished **$51,733 behind doing nothing,** and not because theres anything wrong with it. Gold went from 49 to 408 over that window. Buying a new high and selling the first close under the 50 day hands you a slice of each leg and gives back the rest, 44 times in a row, and the slices dont add up to the move.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

The reason im posting it is the first number on its own. A 1.41 profit factor and a 33% drawdown reads like a working system when its sitting by itself in a results panel, and nothing in it tells you the thing it was trading went up eightfold while you were in and out of it. You only find that out by running the version with no rules in it at all, over the identical window, with the same costs charged.
